name: Haryana: Mera Pani Meri Virasat (Paddy Diversification Incentive)
summary: Haryana pays an incentive per acre to farmers who replace water-guzzling paddy with crops like maize, cotton, bajra, pulses or vegetables, to protect groundwater.

benefits.headline: ₹7,000 per acre incentive for shifting from paddy to alternative crops (confirm the current rate)
details: Incentive is paid per acre by DBT for growing maize, cotton, bajra, pulses, vegetables and other approved alternatives instead of paddy. The state has announced an increase to ₹8,000 per acre, so confirm the current rate.
Related support in the scheme: free seeds, procurement of the alternate crop and a higher subsidy on drip irrigation, as announced by the state.
Agroforestry is also included, with a separate per-acre incentive.

summary: You farm in Haryana and shift (or have shifted) paddy area to an approved alternative crop in the kharif season.
Priority and targets are set for paddy-intensive blocks with falling water tables.
You register your crop details on the state's Meri Fasal Mera Byora / Mera Pani Meri Virasat portal.

You must register before the portal closes; incentives are paid after field verification (physical/ satellite).

steps: Register your land and crop details on the Haryana 'Meri Fasal Mera Byora' (and Mera Pani Meri Virasat) portal in the kharif registration window.
Sow the approved alternative crop instead of paddy on the registered area.
Officials verify your fields. After verification the incentive is credited to your bank account.
offline: Block / district Agriculture office (Haryana Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Department)

deadline.text: Registration is held every kharif season, and the exact dates are announced by the department. Dates shown here are only approximate.

caveats: The incentive amount and the list of targeted blocks change from year to year. Confirm them with your Block Agriculture Officer.
